title: You Don't Need a Driver's License to Travel — Here Is What Every Court Has Actually Said About That.
summary: Consumer-law creator explains why the traveler-not-driver theory always loses and points to Fourth and Fifth Amendment rights and Section 1983 instead.

assertions.quote: is not the right to operate a motor vehicle on public roads without a license
Courts have addressed this specifically and rejected it uniformly.
the court held that the states have the power to regulate the use of motor vehicles on their public roads
Not one court has agreed in over a century of litigation.
People have had their vehicles impounded and when they tried to litigate the theory, they've lost.
It has nothing to do with motor vehicle licensings.

verdicts.note: The UCC governs commercial transactions; licensing rests on state police power statutes.
Maryland had a full motor vehicle licensing and registration statute in 1910, upheld in 1915 as police power, decades before the UCC existed.

assertions.quote: The constitutional right to travel that courts have recognized is the right to move between states as a citizen.

verdicts.note: Crandall, Shapiro and Saenz concern interstate movement and residency, not vehicle operation.
Ohio holds the travel right does not cover driving a car, but also recognizes a fundamental right of intrastate travel, so the 'between states' limit is too narrow.

assertions.quote: In states that have a stop and identify statutes, refusing to identify yourself can be itself be a crime.

verdicts.note: Hiibel v. Sixth Judicial District upheld convictions under state stop-and-identify laws.
Ohio R.C. 2921.29 makes it an offense to refuse name, address or date of birth to an officer with reasonable suspicion; the driver was convicted of it.

assertions.quote: you must explicitly say this. Silence alone is not enough.

verdicts.note: Berghuis v. Thompkins held that a suspect must unambiguously invoke the right to remain silent.

assertions.quote: Courts have held that an officer cannot use your refusal to consent as a basis of a search.

verdicts.note: Consent must be voluntary and courts hold refusal cannot by itself supply probable cause, though other exceptions may still allow a search.

assertions.quote: This documentation plus a civil rights attorney will get you paid.

verdicts.note: Section 1983 is the real remedy, but qualified immunity and litigation costs mean most claims do not pay out.
